items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Stanley Clarke (PHONETIC) never having heard of John Kirby.

ctx.x: But then, too, there's a problem that Chris talks about is there's no guarantee of where they'll go back to. It's like Stanley Clarke (PHONETIC) never having heard of John Kirby. Because the collective improvisation, that approach to playing the fiddle is not taught. There's no guarantee what people will learn or where they'll go.

Well, that's true, but most of them think, "Oh, I know music backwards and forward," you know, that they qualify to play anything. But that's not the way it is really. To play just straight-ahead music. Anybody can write anything for you. They write solos for guys and they can play them. I marvel at the fact that Paul Jeffrey (PHONETIC) give me a record date back there in '72, you know, after you and I met, and Paul did all the arrangements on that. I'm looking at the music; he knew (unintelligible) to write…

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I came out of the mold of Blanton and Israel Crosby ... and a few others -- Truck Chuck Parham (PHONETIC), John Kirby Curved (PHONETIC), oh, even Milt Hinton. Well, they all give me something, you know, with which to grow.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, well, like I said, I came out of the mold of Blanton and Israel Crosby (PROPHETIC) and a few

others -- Truck Chuck Parham (PHONETIC), John Kirby Curved (PHONETIC), oh, even Milt Hinton. Well, they all give me something, you know, with which to grow. I noticed the younger bassists, you hardly hear them mention the great bassists like Paul Chambers, you know, or Ray Brown, for that matter. Most of the young bassists don't say nothing. They hardly say anything about Oscar Pettiford. But most all the youngsters, I can tell that they followed Paul. Paul was the master. He was the master with the bow, but it…

Well, the way I play bass -- I'm speaking about myself -- I'm more percussive. I'd rather the drummer lay out, so I can create something. I know where I'm at mostly at all times, you know, and it's up to the guys around me to know where they at, musically. If they're going to -- if we're playing together and I take a solo and I have them all laying out, they should follow me, you know, know where I'm at. I might play two choruses, but I'm playing two choruses, you know? Whatever.
